newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Sweden says WEU proposal could threaten enlargement.
newsitem.headline: Sweden says WEU proposal could threaten enlargement.

text.p: A six-country proposal to merge the Western European Union and the European Union could threaten EU plans to admit up to 10 members from eastern Europe, Swedish Foreign Minister Lena-Hjelm Wallen was quoted as saying on Monday.

Hjelm-Wallen said she was convinced that Russia, which is opposed to plans to enlarge NATO, would raise the same kind of objections to the enlargement of the EU if it turned into a military alliance, the Swedish news agency TT reported.
This would mean that countries which Russia in practice has accepted as new members of NATO, probably Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic, would have no problems in also joining the EU, TT said.
However, Russian opposition to the three Baltic republics of Estonia, Lithuania and Latvia joining NATO could become an extra obstacle to their EU entry, it said.
It could become fairly complicated for some countries if the EU gets a defence alliance component, TT quoted Hjelm-Wallen as telling journalists during the general affairs council.
She was commenting on a proposal for the gradual incorporation of the WEU defence grouping into the EU proper which is backed by Italy, Germany, Luxembourg, Belgium and Spain.

Hjelm-Wallen warned that the proposal, which has won support from other EU countries, could make enlargement considerably "The EU should be a peace project for the whole of Europe, not only for half of it," she said.
But she declined to say whether Sweden would veto the proposal in the inter-governmental conference (IGC).
Stockholm promised during its EU membership negotiations not to block other countries from forming a defence alliance.

"But France and other countries will not only meet with resistance from Sweden and other non-aligned countries against the proposal," she said, noting that Britain was firmly opposed to all proposals of coordinating the EU and WEU.
